# Lab 1.6: Query BigQuery from Python

## What We Are Going to Do
Use the `google-cloud-bigquery` client library in Cloud Shell to run a parameterised query and load the result into a pandas DataFrame.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Install the libraries.**

<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">pip install --quiet google-cloud-bigquery pandas db-dtypes google-cloud-bigquery-storage</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[CLI] Write the script.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">cat &gt; first_query.py &lt;&lt;'EOF'
from google.cloud import bigquery

client = bigquery.Client()
sql = """
SELECT name, SUM(number) AS total
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
WHERE state = @state
GROUP BY name
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 10
"""
job = client.query(sql, job_config=bigquery.QueryJobConfig(
    query_parameters=[bigquery.ScalarQueryParameter("state", "STRING", "TX")]))
df = job.to_dataframe()
print(df)
print("Job ID:", job.job_id, "| Bytes processed:", job.total_bytes_processed)
EOF
python3 first_query.py</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[Console] Find the Python job.** In Studio, open **Personal history**. Find the job ID printed by the script. Open it and see the parameter `@state = TX` under **Job information**.

4. **[CLI] Change the parameter.** Edit `"TX"` to `"CA"` and run the script again. The second run is a different query, so no cache hit.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Output | Top 10 names in a pandas DataFrame |
| Parameters | Passed safely, not concatenated into SQL |
| Job | Visible in console history with its parameter |
| Auth | Cloud Shell uses your user credentials automatically |
